recommendation: Keep this commit as-is. It restores the published OO decision to the active renamed ObservationDefinition element without changing the accepted Observation wording or opening a broader policy question about declaring cardinality combination semantics elsewhere.
issue_request: FHIR-17787 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for STU3. It asked whether multiple Observation.referenceRange.appliesTo values mean logical AND or OR and noted the same ambiguity for ObservationDefinition.qualifiedInterval.appliesTo. The accepted rule was that repeated Observation.referenceRange instances are OR alternatives, while repeated appliesTo values inside one range or interval are an AND intersection of the target population.
initial_application: The Jira comment identifies commit 49ecb8feb51079b5eb5e34a2f8639078a5d2c3ea as the initial application. That commit added OR wording to Observation.referenceRange and AND wording to Observation.referenceRange.appliesTo in the old spreadsheet source. Current Observation source still carries both clarifications.
additional_context: ObservationDefinition is active in the current build: source/fhir.ini lists ObservationDefinition as a draft resource, maps the observationdefinition folder to the resource, and maps the old ObservationDefinition.qualifiedInterval.appliesTo path to the current ObservationDefinition.qualifiedValue.appliesTo path. A 2021 ObservationDefinition refactor changed qualifiedInterval to qualifiedValue and left the current appliesTo definition without the AND clarification. FHIR-18240 is a duplicate background issue asking the same Observation.referenceRange.appliesTo AND/OR question, and FHIR-53279 is later value-set deduplication background that does not affect appliesTo semantics.
reconciliation: Updated source/observationdefinition/structuredefinition-ObservationDefinition.xml so ObservationDefinition.qualifiedValue.appliesTo states that multiple appliesTo values are interpreted as an AND of the target populations, using the same African American female example already present on Observation.referenceRange.appliesTo. Observation.referenceRange and Observation.referenceRange.appliesTo were not changed because current source already expresses the accepted OR/AND distinction.
source_changes: source/observationdefinition/structuredefinition-ObservationDefinition.xml: clarified that repeated ObservationDefinition.qualifiedValue.appliesTo values are ANDed target-population criteria.

related_jiras.note: Duplicate STU3 issue asking whether multiple Observation.referenceRange.appliesTo values are ANDed or ORed; its comment points back to GF#17787.
Later R6 value-set deduplication across Observation and ObservationDefinition confirms the resources remain coupled, but it does not change appliesTo semantics.
